1. (Currently amended) An aircraft weapons control system comprising: a weapons stores processor panel for receiving input signals from a weapons input; a weapons interface for receiving fire signals from the weapons stores processor panel to control firing of aircraft weapons; and a flight management system in communication with the weapons stores processor panel and the weapons interface, the flight management system providing control signals to the weapons interface; wherein the weapons stores processor panel implements safety interlocks to prevent or enable firing of the aircraft weapons; __wherein the weapons stores processor panel receives real-time threat data from an external threat detection system and modifies the safety interlocks based on the threat data__.

2. (Original)

3. (Original)

4. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the __weapons stores__ processor panel communicates with the weapons interface using a MIL-STD-1760 standard.

5. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a laser pointer coupled to the weapons processor panel; __wherein the laser pointer is integrated with a fire control system that provides targeting data to the weapons stores processor panel independent of the flight management system__.

6. (Original)

7. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the __weapons stores__ processor panel, the control panel including a master arm switch for selecting a master arm position, a safe position and an off position.

11. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 7 wherein: the control panel also includes a laser arm switch for powering a laser pointer through the weapons stores processor panel; __wherein the laser arm switch is mechanically independent from the master arm switch and provides independent control of laser pointer power__.

14. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a weapons select switch which designates a weapon to fire, the weapons select switch including an off position in which the weapons stores processor panel disables fire signals __to__ the weapons interface.

15. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel provides display information for a helmet mounted display, control display unit, and a multifunction function display; __wherein the display information includes real-time weapons status and firing authorization status independent of flight management system inputs__.

16. (Currently amended) The aircraft weapons control system of claim 1 wherein: the weapons stores processor panel provides data for a weapons bus controller to implement firing of weapons; __wherein the weapons stores processor panel implements independent verification of firing commands before transmission to the weapons bus controller__.

17. (Currently amended) A vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) rotary-wing aircraft comprising: an aircraft mounted weapon; and an aircraft weapons control system, the aircraft weapons control system including: a weapons stores processor panel for receiving input signals from a weapons input; a weapons interface for receiving fire signals from the weapons stores processor panel to control firing of the aircraft weapon; and a flight management system in communication with the weapons stores processor panel and the weapons interface, the flight management system providing control signals to the weapons interface; wherein the weapons stores processor panel implements safety interlocks to prevent or enable firing of the aircraft weapon; __wherein the weapons stores processor panel receives real-time threat data from an external threat detection system and modifies the safety interlocks based on the threat data__.

18. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a laser pointer coupled to the weapons stores processor panel; __wherein the laser pointer is integrated with a fire control system that provides targeting data to the weapons stores processor panel independent of the flight management system__.

23. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 19 wherein: the control panel also includes a laser arm switch for powering a laser pointer through the weapons stores processor panel; __wherein the laser arm switch is mechanically independent from the master arm switch and provides independent control of laser pointer power__.

26. (Currently amended) The rotary-wing aircraft of claim 17 further comprising: a control panel on the weapons stores processor panel, the control panel including a weapons select switch which designates a weapon to fire in a manual over-ride mode, the weapons select switch including an off position in which the weapons stores processor panel disables fire signals __to__ the weapons interface.
